newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber- S.E.Asia prices seen stuck in narrow-range.
newsitem.headline: Rubber- S.E.Asia prices seen stuck in narrow-range.

text.p: Southeast Asian prices will probably be mired in a tight range this week with the market deadened by weak demand, traders said on Monday.
"Prices are likely to move in a narrow range. Any falls or rises are likely to be limited. Supply is still tight but there is unlikely to be much demand," one Jakarta-based dealer said.
"Demand is still not there. The situation does not look encouraging for any upward movement in prices," a Singapore-based rubber trader said.
Another Indonesian dealer said market talk that China was planning to enter the market in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand was not likely to have much impact on the regional market.
"Unless the Chinese enter the market in a big way, then they would not make a difference to the market," he said.
Thai dealers said that although Chinese buyers checked on prices last week, they filed no fresh orders.
"We've been hearing the Chinese talk for a while, but supplies continue to pile up and demand remains on the weak side. Prices will probably trend lower for now," a rubber trader in Singapore added.

Indonesian dealers said SIR20 offer prices for October deliveries are likely to remain stable between 56.50-57.50 U.S. cents/lb FOB Medan, 56.25-57.25 cents FOB Palembang, Surabaya and Padang, and at 56.00-57.00 cents FOB Jambi and Pontianak.
SIR10, meanwhile, is forecast to be on offer for 0.25-0.50 cents/lb higher than the SIR20, they said, adding demand for SIR20 was seen remaining weak.
Shoe-grade SIR3L is also seen remaining weak due to a lack of fresh demand, dealer said.
SIR3L was on offer between 137.5 cents/kg-138.00 cents/kg. The grade last traded at 136.00 cents/kg for October deliveries FOB Lampung against the previous 137.0 cents.
High amoniac latex remained on offer at 2,260 rupiah/kg in Tangerang and Bandung against the previous 2,350 rupiah.
In Thailand, nearby rubber prices were steady last week, despite a drop in supply, as demand remained soft.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for October shipment was quoted around US$1.28-1.29/kg, barely changed from the previous week.
A recent wet spell in the main southern and other growing areas last week trimmed supplies, traders said.
Rubber prices in Malaysia, however, were expected to firm up this week as producers had been extremely reluctant to sell at lower levels, traders said.
"I think factories have come to a stage where they'd rather not process rubber than sell below their production cost," a one dealer said.
The benchmark October RSS1 closed at Malaysian 329 cents a kg on Friday, while SMR20 ended last week at 314 cents a kg.
"I still see the market's upside potential more than the downside this week," said a dealer, adding Malaysian prices could nudge up between two and three cents.
(With contributions from Kuala Lumpur, Jakarta and Bangkok)
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
